title: Reflect-then-Correct: Rebalancing Task Optimization for Generalizable Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Distributional Value Error Reduction
claim: A multi-module learning system composes task inference, distributional value learning, and error-driven reweighting, with a zoomed-in view of its key subroutine.
layout: 3 modules left-to-right plus zoomed side panel; color-coded modules, gray zoom wedge
description: A wide framework diagram split into three color-coded modules plus a zoom-in panel. On the left, a blue Module A (Task Inference) takes training-task thumbnails (robot manipulation scenes) through a Context Encoder, producing a latent z that feeds a Decoder and a Policy. The center top, in orange, is Module B (Sinkhorn Distributional Meta-Value Learning). Meta-Value and Target Meta-Value networks output scatter-plot particle clouds, which go into a Sinkhorn Block, then a Sinkhorn TD Error box, then the loss L_phi. The center bottom, in green, is Module C (Error Correction). An Error Model and a Target Error Model feed an Exp Map and Importance Weights, shown with a balance-scale icon. A green arrow carries the weighted update back to the loss. A right-hand peach panel, linked by a gray wedge, expands the Sinkhorn Block: cost matrix, iterated scaling vectors, optimal transport matrix, and cost D, with small heatmap icons.
caption: Framework of RTC. Module A (Task Inference) encodes trajectories to infer task representations z for conditioning the policy
abstract: Meta-Reinforcement Learning (Meta-RL) faces significant challenges in non-parametric settings, where vastly different return scales across diverse tasks cause severe gradient interference. Existing categorical solutions attempt to normalize these scales but often fail due to rigid discretization and quantization errors. To address this, we propose Reflect-then-Correct (RTC), a framework that models meta-values using Sinkhorn divergence. By treating distributions as adaptive floating particles, RTC achieves a geometry-aware alignment of distinct meta-task structures. However, while Sinkhorn updates harmonize gradients, they introduce statistical bias via sampling estimation. RTC overcomes this issue by "reflecting'' on the temporal accumulation of Bellman inconsistencies through a recursive error model and "correcting'' the optimization via adaptive importance weights, which prioritize more accurate transitions for meta-value estimation. We provide theoretical guarantees for this reweighting strategy and demonstrate that RTC outperforms existing baselines on the challenging Meta-World ML-10 and ML-45 benchmarks.
